CVE-2026-94266.8e8a4d700b8600f4cc54dc33efe7aabeae0fe959:
Supply git credentials through a credential helper instead of the clone URL (#16862) (#16864)

* Supply git credentials through a credential helper instead of the clone URL

libcurl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.30 (CVE-2026-94266) strips credentials from
CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL. git uses it to follow redirects, so a clone whose URL
embeds credentials and whose repository URL redirects loses them on the
follow-up request and fails with 'could not read Username ... expected flush
after ref listing'. dbt deps passes the rendered package URL, credentials
included, straight to git clone.

Split http(s) credentials out of the URL and supply them through a git
credential helper configured with GIT_CONFIG_* env vars, scoped to the
repository's origin. git only calls a helper after a 401, like URL credentials,
so public repositories with a placeholder token behave as before (an
Authorization header would not: it is sent up front and GitHub rejects an
invalid one). The credentials stay out of argv, the logged command and the
clone's .git/config. Applied to clone, sparse-checkout and fetch.

Resolves #16861



* Keep credentials out of git error messages and shorten comments

GitCloningError, GitCheckoutError, UnknownGitCloningProblemError and the
'never saw Cloning into' error still interpolated the original URL, token
included. Use the credential-free URL, and pass the auth env to run_cmd
directly instead of falling back to None at each call site.



* Assert the credential given to git, not the clone URL, in secret scrubbing test

CVE-2024-22195.b2270fa38ad76d096029c59cbf9d43f22ba001a8:
[Backport 1.5.latest] Upgrade Jinja2 dependency version specification to address CVE-2024-22195 (#9670)

* Upgrade Jinja2 dependency version specification to address CVE-2024-22195 (#9638)

CVE-2024-22195 identified an issue in Jinja2 versions <= 3.1.2. As such
we've gone and changed our dependency requirement specification to be
3.1.3 or greater (but less than 4).

Note: Preivously we were using the `~=` version specifier. However due
to some issues with the `~=` we've moved to using `>=` in combination
with `<`. This gives us the same range that `~=` gave us, but avoids
a pip resolution issue when multiple packages in an environment use `~=`
for the same dependency.
